setup: Sit in the leg press, back flat on the pad
Balls of your feet on the platform's bottom edge
Heels hanging off; knees straight but not locked
Keep the safety catches in place if it allows
execution: Push through the balls of your feet
Point your toes as far as you can and pause
Lower slowly into a calf stretch
Keep your knees still the whole time
faults: Don't bend your knees to help push
Don't bounce out of the stretch

notes: Your feet are near the platform's edge. If they slip, the platform can come down toward you, so start light, wear shoes with grip, and use the machine's safety catches or stops if it has them.
Keep your knees soft but still; only the ankles move.
The logged load is the plates added (or the stack reading on a stack leg press). It isn't comparable with a standing calf raise or another machine.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view of a 45° leg press at hip height, figure's head on the left. Feet on the lower edge of the platform with the heels hanging off; the ankle must be large and clear in frame.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Seated in the leg press, back on the pad, legs nearly straight. Balls of the feet on the platform's bottom edge, heels dropped below it, ankles bent for a calf stretch.

keyPositions.label: Pointed
keyPositions.describe: Ankles extended, toes pushing the platform away. Knees unchanged; only the platform and feet have moved.

ikHints: Hips and back fixed on the seat
Balls of the feet fixed on the platform edge; platform moves along its rails
emphasise: Only the ankles move; knees stay still
Heels drop below the edge, then the toes point

uncertain.note: Added (plates) by default, matching the 45° leg press entry. On a seated stack leg press it's a stack reading; an import or Ben picks which.
Neither source mentions safety catches. Whether the catches can stay engaged depends on the machine; the safety note is reasoned from the foot position, not sourced.
"Calf press" can also mean a dedicated seated calf-press machine. It is the same movement, so it stays an alias, but loads aren't comparable between machines.
Approximate drawing targets, not measured data. Negative ankleDorsiflexion means the ankle is pointed.
